title: Impact of Rent Control Expansion on Urban Rental Prices

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Difference-in-Differences (two-way fixed effects).
- Why: We observe panel data for districts (unit_id) over time (period) with a treatment that turns on in the post period for treated districts. DID with unit and period fixed effects nets out time-invariant district heterogeneity and common time shocks, isolating the causal effect of the policy on log rents.
- Key assumptions:
  - Parallel trends: In the absence of the rent control expansion, treated and control districts would have followed similar trends in log rents.
  - No anticipatory effects: Treated districts do not adjust rents before the policy becomes active.
  - Stable treatment and no spillovers: Treatment in one district does not affect outcomes in control districts.
  - Composition is stable and measurement consistent across periods.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Complete, self-contained R code

# 0) Packages
pkgs <- c("data.table", "fixest")
for (p in pkgs) {
  if (!requireNamespace(p, quietly = TRUE)) install.packages(p)
}
library(data.table)
library(fixest)

# 1) Read data
path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s38_data.csv"
df <- fread(path)

# Basic checks and preparation
df[, unit_id := as.factor(unit_id)]
df[, period  := as.integer(period)]
df[, treated := as.integer(treated)]
df[, post    := as.integer(post)]
df[, treat_x_post := as.integer(treat_x_post)]
# y is already numeric (log rent)

cat("Data loaded. N =", nrow(df), 
    " | #units =", length(unique(df$unit_id)),
    " | #periods =", length(unique(df$period)), "\n")

# 2) Main DID: TWFE with clustering at the unit level
m_twfe <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period, data = df, cluster = ~unit_id)

b <- coef(m_twfe)["treat_x_post"]
se <- se(m_twfe)["treat_x_post"]
p  <- pvalue(m_twfe)["treat_x_post"]
att_pct <- 100*(exp(b) - 1)

cat("\nMain DID (TWFE, cluster by unit):\n")
cat("  Coef (treat_x_post) =", round(b, 4), 
    " | SE =", round(se, 4),
    " | p-value =", round(p, 4), "\n")
cat("  Implied % effect on rents =", round(att_pct, 2), "%\n")

# 3) Robustness A: Two-way clustered standard errors (unit and period)
m_twfe_2w <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period, data = df, cluster = ~unit_id + period)

b2 <- coef(m_twfe_2w)["treat_x_post"]
se2 <- se(m_twfe_2w)["treat_x_post"]
p2  <- pvalue(m_twfe_2w)["treat_x_post"]
att_pct2 <- 100*(exp(b2) - 1)

cat("\nRobustness A (TWFE, two-way clustering unit & period):\n")
cat("  Coef (treat_x_post) =", round(b2, 4), 
    " | SE =", round(se2, 4),
    " | p-value =", round(p2, 4), "\n")
cat("  Implied % effect on rents =", round(att_pct2, 2), "%\n")

# 4) Robustness B: Event-study to inspect dynamics and pre-trends
# Identify base (last pre) period
if (any(df$post == 0)) {
  base_t <- max(df$period[df$post == 0])
} else {
  # If no explicit pre period marked, take the second smallest as base (fallback)
  base_t <- sort(unique(df$period))[2]
}

# Create treated x period interactions excluding the base period
all_periods <- sort(unique(df$period))
es_terms <- c()
for (t in all_periods) {
  if (t == base_t) next
  varname <- paste0("D_", t)
  df[[varname]] <- as.integer(df$period == t & df$treated == 1)
  es_terms <- c(es_terms, varname)
}

# Fit event-study (unit & period FE); cluster at unit
es_formula <- as.formula(paste("y ~", paste(es_terms, collapse = " + "), "| unit_id + period"))
m_es <- feols(es_formula, data = df, cluster = ~unit_id)

ct <- confint(m_es, level = 0.95)
coefs <- coef(m_es)

# Separate pre and post period coefficients relative to base
pre_t  <- all_periods[all_periods < base_t]
post_t <- all_periods[all_periods > base_t]

pre_names  <- paste0("D_", pre_t)
post_names <- paste0("D_", post_t)

# Helper to print ES coefficients cleanly
print_es <- function(names_vec, label) {
  if (length(names_vec) == 0) {
    cat(paste0("  No ", label, " coefficients (check data).\n"))
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  cat(paste0("  ", label, " coefficients (relative to period ", base_t, "):\n"))
  for (nm in names_vec) {
    if (nm %in% names(coefs)) {
      b  <- coefs[nm]
      se <- se(m_es)[nm]
      lb <- ct[nm, 1]; ub <- ct[nm, 2]
      pct <- 100*(exp(b) - 1)
      cat("   ", nm, ": beta =", round(b, 4), 
          "| SE =", round(se, 4),
          "| 95% CI [", round(lb, 4), ",", round(ub, 4), "]",
          "| % =", round(pct, 2), "%\n")
    }
  }
  # Summary stat: mean absolute pre or post effect
  vals <- coefs[names_vec]
  cat("   Mean(abs(beta)) =", round(mean(abs(vals), na.rm = TRUE), 4), "\n")
}

cat("\nRobustness B (Event-study with unit & period FE; cluster by unit):\n")
print_es(pre_names,  "Pre")
print_es(post_names, "Post")

# 5) Additional check: Simple two-way FE but report sample means to benchmark
# (No estimation change; just sanity check of treatment intensity and timing)
cat("\nSanity checks:\n")
cat("  Treated share =", round(mean(df$treated), 3), 
    " | Post share =", round(mean(df$post), 3), "\n")
cat("  Mean log rent (pre, control)  =", round(mean(df$y[df$post==0 & df$treated==0]), 4), "\n")
cat("  Mean log rent (pre, treated)  =", round(mean(df$y[df$post==0 & df$treated==1]), 4), "\n")
cat("  Mean log rent (post, control) =", round(mean(df$y[df$post==1 & df$treated==0]), 4), "\n")
cat("  Mean log rent (post, treated) =", round(mean(df$y[df$post==1 & df$treated==1]), 4), "\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Negative. Rent control expansion should reduce average observed log rental prices in treated districts relative to control, at least in the short run, due to binding caps on covered units.
- Magnitude: Roughly -0.05 to -0.10 in logs (about -5% to -10%). The exact effect depends on the coverage share and supply-side responses; short-run effects typically skew negative, while longer-term general equilibrium effects may attenuate or even reverse for uncovered stock, but with district-level averages we expect a modest negative ATT.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare changes in log rental prices over time between treated and untreated districts.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The expansion of rent control policies led to a decrease in log rental prices in treated districts.
